Basic Usage ​

Analyze text, create an SVG, and save it to a file:

javascript
const WriteLikeMe = require('@ai-clyde/writelikeme');
const fs = require('fs');

const text = 'A sample paragraph to inspect.';
const profile = WriteLikeMe.analyzeText(text);
const svg = WriteLikeMe.generateStyleSVG(profile);

console.log(profile);
const generatedDraft = 'A draft produced by your AI integration.';
console.log(WriteLikeMe.compareTextStyle(text, generatedDraft));
fs.writeFileSync('writelikeme-code.svg', svg);

const sharedProfile = WriteLikeMe.readStyleCode(svg);
const localDraft = WriteLikeMe.writeLikeMe(
  'Write a short paragraph about community gardens.',
  sharedProfile
);
console.log(localDraft);

compareTextStyle gives an experimental style-match score and per-signal differences that an AI integration can use to review or refine its draft. readStyleCode restores the JSON profile embedded in the SVG, and writeLikeMe uses it to make a deterministic draft locally. The built-in writer does not call an AI service and has limited ability to follow complex prompts.

The analyzer uses simple text-shape and English keyword heuristics. Results are experimental rather than AI assessments. See the analyzeText API reference before interpreting the scores.

The published entry point is CommonJS, not a standalone browser script. Use a frontend build tool that supports CommonJS dependencies to include it in a browser application.
